entityDescription: The European Forest Institute (EFI) is a pan-European international organization. It has 29 Member Countries, and appr. 130 member organizations from appr. 40 different countries working in diverse research fields. EFI provides forest-related knowledge around three interconnected and interdisciplinary themes: bioeconomy, resilience and governance. With a staff of over 100 experts in several offices across Europe, EFI is in a unique position to generate, connect and share knowledge at the interface between science and policy. EFI excels in carrying out projects at the European level, and has a track record of over 30 projects carried out for the European Commission DGs during the past few years. EFI puts increasing emphasis on cross-sectoral approaches in its research and development activities. It is thus in a good position to have efficient access to social, economic and environmental expertise covering all of Europe’s bio-geographical regions. The work in the field of policy support includes enhanced support for decision takers and policy makers. For example, the high-level forum on forests, ThinkForest, brings together high-level policy makers and leading European forest scientists to generate science-policy dialogue on strategic forest-related issues. EFI is quickly becoming a leading science-policy platform providing forest-related knowledge to build a sustainable future: connecting knowledge to action. www.efi.int

entityDescription:
The Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg (OVGU) was founded in 1993 and is one of the youngest German universities. It was formed in a merger of three existing institutions to create a university with a distinctive profile, so that in many areas it is able to draw on a considerably longer tradition. It is located in Magdeburg, the capital city of the federal state Saxony-Anhalt. The University comprises 9 faculties and almost 13,200 students. 

Otto von Guericke Universitaet Magdeburg has a distinctive profile. It aims to create a lean and sharply-defined structure with its main focus of expertise in the traditional areas of engineering, the natural sciences and medicine. It also views economics and management and the social sciences and humanities as essential disciplines for a modern university in the information age. 
The most prominent areas of research emphasis are the neurosciences, dynamic systems in process engineering and biomedicine, plus automotive/digital engineering. In addition, transfer-related areas of emphasis include medical technology, renewable energies, fluidised bed technology, research into dementia, computational visualistics and experimental economics. 
Affiliated institutes and the University's Transfer and Entrepreneur Center act as links between academia and industry. They facilitate businesses' access to the University's research resources while simultaneously promoting innovation. The Faculty of Medicine and University Clinic, which are located on their own campus, are the “educational home” to around 1300 trainee doctors.

entityDescription:
The Fondazione Edmund Mach (FEM) is a leading Italian institution active in research, technology, and technology transfer related to the agro-food sector. FEM is a public agency under private law jurisdiction. FEM comprises a Research and Innovation Centre (CRI), a Training and Education Centre, and a Technology Transfer Centre, all carrying out activities in the fields of agro-food and sustainable development. Currently, FEM makes up a full-scale rural centre stretching out over a 14-hectare campus, with classrooms, greenhouses, offices. FEM owns 120 hectares of land cultivated with apple and grape and 80ha of forests. Nowadays around 800 students attend classes, assisted by over 100teachers. 58% of FEM personnel are males. The majority of collaborators are 30-50 years old. 15% percent is of foreign nationality. The Edmund Mach Foundation is organized into Centers geared to the specific aims of: 1. Education and Training (CIF); 2. Research and Innovation (CRI); 3. Technical Experimentation and Transfer (CTT). Today, the goal of improving the characteristics and potential of agriculture is reached through the integration between the school, the Research and Innovation Centre (CRI), and the technical support provided to companies and farms. FEM promotes and enhances, through research and innovation, the Trentino-land based economy in Italy, aiming at the improvement of agricultural and forestry productions and the improvement of the quality and nutritional value of food products. It also supports the region’s environmental resources through the development and promotion of low-impact agricultural practices, the study and preservation of biodiversity and the characterization of the alpine and subalpine ecosystems.FEM expresses research capacities at the highest international and national levels, as witnessed by a third-party official evaluation in 2022 (ANVUR): FEM ranked 18th (out of 65) in chemistry, 7th in agricultural and veterinary sciences (out of 39), and 3rd (out of 75) in biology, at the national level, when compared with all the involved institution. FEM ranked 4th overall within the above mentioned scientific groups when compared to homologous institutions.

In the coming 3 years (from 2022 to 2025) FEM will play a pivotal role at National level in the deployment of the activities related to research within the EU Recovery Funds and EU Green Deal framework. FEM will be involved in 3 major initiatives. In the National Research Centre for Agricultural Technologies (Agritech) aiming to generate Key Enabling Technologies, it will act particularly in the field of crop genetics and development of more resilient varieties. Within the National Biodiversity Future Center, FEM will favour the use of innovative approaches for biodiversity conservation, with a particular focus on water and terresterial ecosystems in the alpine area
From 2018 to 2022, more than 100 research projects have been granted to CRI researchers (of which more than 40 granted by the EU), both as partners or coordinators. About 50 projects were financed by the European Union
